title: Understanding Your Paramedic Salary NSW: Hourly to Annual with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert your paramedic salary NSW hourly rate to annual pay. Includes 38-hour week, casual loading, super on top, tax estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a paramedic salary NSW, assuming a 38-hour week, your annual gross is hourly rate × 38 × 52. Casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base rate, and super is paid on top of ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual paramedic salary NSW from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week then by 52 weeks. For example, $40/hour gives $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 gross. If you receive casual loading, add 25% to the base rate first.

faqs.q: Does the paramedic salary NSW include casual loading and super?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of your base hourly rate if you are a casual employee. Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it.

faqs.q: What is the average paramedic salary NSW according to official data?
faqs.a: The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for New South Wales full-time adult ordinary time is $2,108.80 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all occupations, not a median for paramedics specifically. For paramedic-specific rates, refer to your award or enterprise agreement.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Paramedic Salary NSW Hourly Rate to Annual

If you're a paramedic in New South Wales, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your super. The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week, which is the full-time ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. For example, if your base hourly rate is $45, your annual gross would be $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

To see your fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same $45/hour example, weekly pay is $1,710, so fortnightly is $3,420. This can help you match your pay cycle.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Many paramedics work as casuals, especially in the early stages of their career. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. On this site, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to the rate you enter. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

For a paramedic salary NSW, if your base rate is $45/hour, the casual rate becomes $45 × 1.25 = $56.25/hour. Your annual gross then becomes $56.25 × 38 × 52 = $111,150. This higher figure reflects the compensation for not receiving paid leave.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% for 2026–27, and it applies to your base rate plus any casual loading (if applicable). Super is not deducted from your pay; your employer pays it separately. However, super stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For most paramedics, this cap won't apply.

For more details on casual loading, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page. To understand how super interacts with your pay, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income between $18,201 and $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income.

Using the $45/hour base rate example ($88,920 gross), your estimated tax would be:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $43,920 ($45,001–$88,920) = $13,176
- Total tax = $17,196
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,778.40
- Estimated take-home = $88,920 – $17,196 – $1,778.40 = $69,945.60

Note: This estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a more personalised estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Average Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time in New South Wales as $2,108.80 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for paramedics specifically. Your paramedic salary NSW may differ based on your award, enterprise agreement, experience, and location. For industry-specific benchmarks, refer to [average pay](/topics/average-pay) or [job pay](/topics/job-pay).

### Important Considerations

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour for a 38-hour week ($1,004.90/week). Casual employees get $33.05/hour including 25% loading. Most paramedics earn above this, but it's a useful baseline.
- **Award Rates**: Paramedics are often covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award or an enterprise agreement. These may specify higher minimum rates, penalty rates, and allowances. Check your [pay guides](/blog) for details.
- **Casual vs Permanent**: Permanent employees receive paid leave but no casual loading. Casual loading compensates for the lack of leave entitlements.
- **Super on Top**: Remember, super is paid on top of your gross earnings. The 12% is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional contribution.

For a full breakdown of how your hourly rate converts to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, use [the timesheet](/) on our home page. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for quick comparisons.

### Final Thoughts

Understanding your paramedic salary NSW involves more than just multiplying by 38 and 52. Casual loading, super, and tax all affect your real earnings. Use the tools on this site to experiment with different rates and scenarios. Always refer to your specific award or agreement for the most accurate figures.

For more information, visit [about the timesheet](/about) or [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) to see how your pay compares to legal minimums.
